partial.reason: the phone, tablet and Web browser paths are built (the browser path by #704, Q398 and Q399). Two states are not drawn as the design draws them. Expired and after a problem, the design hides the kind picker and Show a pairing code and puts Show another inside the problem box as its action; the card keeps the picker and relabels its code button Show another above the box, and the expired box has no action. The design draws a reach or certificate problem from what the card knows before any code is asked for; the card computes a problem only from the address an issued code carries, so it spends a code to learn that a device could not reach or trust the daemon. The two absent evidence entries hold those lines of pairing-card.tsx

partial.reason: The card draws what it knows. Its mono line is the daemon's own problem, or Tailscale's own words with no tailnet, not a fixed line. It cannot know that the tailnet address works. Turning the switch on restarts the daemon once, so the still line says that rather than that nothing else changes. The turning-off state is drawn by the Settings card, not the pairing card. The HTTPS line is the longer design line both cards share.

humanRead.note: Phase titles, reach lines and outcome lines are in the component's data; read them against the component.
The design's open question on the unbuilt grant line is settled: phoneAndTabletPromise now says Terminal output is not on a phone yet., the design's line, word for word.

Q347 A: the locked state's mono line pair.issue refused · watch_only_client names a method and code that do not exist; it becomes device.issueCode refused · watching-only credential, a ruled difference from the drawn copy.

Q398 and Q399 (picked 2026-10-02, confirmed by fetzy the same day), differ from the drawn browser QR: the Web browser tab draws no QR, even when the daemon has a webAppUrl, and says to type the code into the web page, showing webAppUrl as text when there is one. Separately, Copy follows the design's own browser instruction (Open the address in the browser and type the code.) and hands over the code alone. The drawn browser QR would be scanned by a phone camera, whose browser greets as a phone or tablet, so a web-kind code would always end in a kind mismatch and an extra paired device. Built by #704 (merge 0595a1bd).

Open gaps in the code slot, apart from the Web browser path (see the Q398 and Q399 note). The card learns of a loopback-only or certificate problem only after spending a code. Its problem box draws the tailnet actions since TailnetReach landed (pairing-card.reach, 2026-10-02); Show another is the code button's own label after a problem or an expiry, not an action inside the box as the design draws it, and Open Machines belongs to the refusal states, which wait on pairing-card.done's protocol block. The line The same code as domovoid pair --client <kind> names a command that prints usage and fails without --label. Q336 A is built: printedCommand draws the linked name, its ~/.local/bin path, or the bundled launcher's full path, so a DMG install no longer names a domovoid that is not on PATH.

Differs from the drawn line on purpose, settling the --label gap the 2026-10-03 note names. The design draws The same code as domovoid pair --client <kind>, which domovoid refuses without --label. On the Phone and Tablet tabs the card keeps the drawn look and words and prints domovoid pair --client phone --label Phone or --client tablet --label Tablet, so the line runs as printed (Q336 A). A placeholder such as <device label> was not used: a copied line would fail in a shell, where < is a redirection. The Web browser tab draws no command line, though the design draws one: domovoid pair --client web --label Browser prints a QR and a domovoi-pair: payload, and the browser's connect page takes the bare word code alone, so no command gives a browser the same code until domovoid pair prints the bare code for web. Superseded by the 2026-10-10 note: since #767 --label is optional and domovoid pair --client web prints the bare word code.

Back to the drawn line on every tab, superseding the 2026-10-07 note and the --label line of the 2026-10-03 open-gaps note. Since #767 (merge 640ac4e7) domovoid pair takes --label as an optional suggested name, and with --client web it prints Web code: and the bare word code, which the browser's connect page takes, rather than a QR and a domovoi-pair: payload. The reason Q25 A gave for drawing no command on the Web browser tab is gone, so the card prints The same code as domovoid pair --client phone, --client tablet or --client web, each running as printed (Q336 A), with no --label.

The Web browser path landed with #704 (merge 0595a1bd): a browser code draws no QR, the slot says No QR for a browser. Type the code there., the code column says to open this address and type the code and shows webAppUrl as text when the daemon has one, and Copy hands over the bare code. The entry stays partial for the two open gaps the 2026-10-03 open-gaps note names first, now held as evidence: Show another inside the box, and a problem known before a code is spent.

Read in Chromium against a fixture with no daemon and no Tailscale: a loopback code with the switch off leads to the setting, which scrolls the Settings card into view and marks it for 1.6 seconds; a code with no trusted certificate asks Tailscale through the switch. The titles name the device kind chosen, so "a phone" reads "a tablet" or "a browser on another device" there.
